bullets.title: MU: Blowout Q3 beat with 16 Strategic Customer Agreements covering $100B+ revenue floor
bullets.body: Micron reported F3Q26 revenue of $41.46B vs consensus $35.91B, non-GAAP EPS $25.11 vs $20.86, and gross margin 84.9% vs 81.7%; guided F4Q26 to $50B revenue/$31 EPS/$86 GM—all well above Street. The company disclosed 16 long-term Strategic Customer Agreements (SCAs) covering ~20% of DRAM and 33% of NAND volume through 2030, with $100B+ minimum cumulative revenue at price floors described as 'well above prior cycle peak margins (~61-86% GM)'; $22B in customer cash deposits secured. Memory supply expected to remain tight beyond CY27 with no line-of-sight on when demand meets supply. PTs broadly raised: Citi $1,400, Wolfe $1,500, UBS $1,625, JPM $1,540, KeyBanc $1,600; company committing to return 100% of excess cash to shareholders starting Dec 9, 2026. Stock rallied ~16-18% post-earnings.

bullets.title: AAPL: Raises Mac/iPad prices 15-25% on memory costs; demand destruction risk flagged
bullets.body: Apple announced price increases of 15-25% across MacBooks, iPads, HomePods, and accessories citing surging memory/NAND costs from AI data center demand; iPhone prices were not raised. Most analysts note Apple's higher memory BOM costs (~$200 additional per iPhone implied), while bulls cite demand inelasticity via carrier/installment plans and record margins. Stock fell ~6% on announcement—worst single-day drop since April 2025. KGI Securities downgraded to Neutral; multiple analysts noted the magnitude exceeded prior mid-single-digit increase expectations.

bullets.title: AVGO: OpenAI 'Jalapeño' custom inference chip unveiled; validates XPU diversification thesis
bullets.body: Broadcom and OpenAI unveiled 'Jalapeño,' OpenAI's first custom LLM inference processor, showing 'substantially better performance per watt than current state-of-the-art.' JPM flagged AVGO receives $15/GW silicon content vs $11/GW for TPU, with Jalapeño shipments expected to exceed 1.3GW. MS also notes MediaTek (not AVGO) won additional Google TPU v9 slots, raising competitive questions. AVGO is also JPM's top pick alongside MU in AI supply chain.

bullets.title: NVDA: Chips doubling in price on China black market; Vera Rubin ramp on track
bullets.body: NVDA DGX B300 server/RTX 6000 Pro chips reportedly more than doubling in price on China's black market amid smuggling crackdowns and strong demand, with B300 servers at ~$1M (CNY7M). NVDA supply chain contacts dismissed Vera Rubin doubts per MS TMT; GB300 transition on track for 3Q26 ramp. CoWoS capacity expected at 200k wafers/month by YE27, with NVDA consuming 1,222k units in 2027 (+57% YoY). Stock was down ~8.6% week-over-week as part of broader Mag 7 selloff.

bullets.title: SNDK/WDC: NAND tight through CY27; SNDK PT raised to $2,500; WDC down 21% on week
bullets.body: Citi raised SNDK PT to $2,500 (Buy; 90-day upside catalyst watch) citing tight NAND supply expected beyond CY27 with CY26 industry bit shipments +20%. Micron's blowout implies NAND ASPs +mid-80% QoQ. Analyst Klein prefers STX/WDC for HDD upside ($80-100 STX, $50-60 WDC EPS by CY27/28 on HAMR pricing). WDC fell 21.4% on the week despite +240% YTD performance—attributed to momentum unwind and Korean ETF-driven flows, not fundamentals.

bullets.title: ACN: Downgraded at TD Cowen to Hold after bookings miss; PT cut 42% to $150
bullets.body: Accenture guided FY26 revenue growth down to +3-4% from +3-5%, and managed services bookings declined -15% YoY well below investor expectations of +4-5%—dragging IT Services peers INFY and others. TD Cowen downgraded to Hold from Buy, cutting PT to $150 from $258. Mizuho lowered PT 19% to $226. UBS maintained Buy at $275 citing ACN's $2B buyback boost (total $7.5B, ~10% of market cap) as confidence signal; stock at 8.5x 2-year forward P/E, lowest in 20+ years.

bullets.title: GOOGL: -5-8% on week as DeepMind AI researchers depart; joins Dow replacing VZ
bullets.body: Multiple high-profile AI researchers departed Google DeepMind for rivals: Nobel laureate John Jumper (AlphaFold) left for Anthropic, and Noam Shazeer (Gemini co-lead) left for OpenAI. Google also delayed Gemini 3.5 Pro launch to July. Despite talent losses, CEO Hassabis publicly downplayed concerns. Positively, GOOGL will replace VZ in the DJIA effective June 29. Stock fell ~5% on June 23 and ~8.3% on the week, becoming a 'source of funds' for the semi rotation.

bullets.title: DKNG: Launches DKeX proprietary prediction markets exchange; June PM volumes $200M+ annualized at $11.3B
bullets.body: DraftKings launched DKeX, completing its vertically integrated prediction market stack. June consumer PM volumes tracking $200M+, up 80% from May's $110M. For the week of June 21, annualized total trading volume was $11.3B ($3.4B consumer-facing, $7.9B market-making). JPM reiterated Overweight, noting PM LTVs tracking similar to traditional OSB customers. Citizens raised PT to $36 from $34 and suggested PM opportunity may exceed current market cap. Stock +6.5% on DKeX announcement.

bullets.title: CCL: 2Q beat on costs; FY26 yield guidance cut 100bps to +1.75% on Mid-East headwinds
bullets.body: Carnival reported Q2 adj. EPS of $0.41 vs $0.33 consensus, beating on significant cost outperformance (+0.1% net cruise costs ex-fuel vs +2.6% guide). But FY26 yield guidance was cut 100bps to +1.75% constant currency due to prolonged Middle East conflict impact on European bookings; Q3 yield guided +1.2% well below Street's +2.8%. Management noted June bookings 'turned a corner' and 2027 European bookings running mid-teens% ahead of prior year. UBS/JPM both reiterate Buy with $35-$43 PTs, characterizing headwinds as transitory.

bullets.title: NFLX: Down 5-6% on META competition and engagement data; Wolfe initiates at Outperform $107
bullets.body: Netflix fell ~6% on June 22 driven by reports of slower global net adds in alternative data and Meta's announced expansion into long-form episodic content on Instagram TV. Nielsen data also showed NFLX watch time down from 100 min/day to 93 min/day while YouTube rose to 99. Separately, Wolfe Research initiated NFLX at Outperform with $107 PT (28x 2027E EPS), arguing 19x forward P/E represents a compelling entry given 15% revenue CAGR, 32% OI margins, and strongest net retention score (+18) in Morgan Stanley's streaming survey. OMC also announced AI ad collaboration with NFLX.

bullets.title: ORCL: Down 19.4% on week, largest counterparty exposure to OpenAI IPO delay
bullets.body: Oracle fell 19.4% on the week amid OpenAI's IPO delay to 2027 and concerns about ORCL's outsized counterparty risk. Separately, Oracle also cut ~21,000 employees (~13% of workforce) in an AI-driven restructuring. KeyBanc raised FY28-FY30 EPS estimates above consensus, maintaining Overweight at $300 PT, citing opex moderation offsetting AI margin pressure. OpenAI delaying IPO due to inability to achieve $1T valuation target and cautious market conditions.

bullets.title: MSFT: Technical score 0 per 22V; Italy launches antitrust probe over Microsoft 365 pricing
bullets.body: 22V Research assigned MSFT its worst Technical Score (0/4), noting the stock is below its declining 200-day MA since February 2026, down 18% from early June highs, with support at 350-355 that could break toward $250. Italian Competition Authority launched investigation into Microsoft over unfair commercial practices related to Microsoft 365 price increases, citing unclear disclosures about Copilot integration. MSFT also raised Xbox prices a third time in 13 months ($100-$150 increase) citing memory/storage costs up 2.5x.

bullets.title: T/VZ: Dominate AWS-3 spectrum reauction at $3.56B; AT&T raises admin fee $1/line
bullets.body: Verizon won 82 licenses for $3.2B, T-Mobile 102 licenses for $277.8M, and AT&T 120.8M in FCC Auction 113, with national MNOs winning 194/200 licenses (~99.5% of proceeds). Separately, AT&T raised its Administrative & Regulatory Cost Recovery fee from $3.99 to $4.99/line/month effective August 5 on ~75M postpaid lines—KeyBanc estimates ~$900M annualized revenue uplift with minimal churn risk, maintained Overweight at $36 PT.

bullets.title: FIG: Config 2026 showcases Intelligent Canvas; Citi upgrades to Buy at $36 PT
bullets.body: Figma's Config 2026 event introduced Code Layers, Motion, Shaders, and AI agent-assisted tools; Citi upgraded to Buy with $36 PT (93% upside from $18.64) citing broader platform expansion driving seat upgrades and credit consumption. However, Wolfe maintained Peer Perform—noting Figma Make received mixed reviews, AI usage remains a minority of seats, and new features carry near-term gross margin headwinds during beta. JPM noted neutral on FIG with concerns about beta monetization timing.

bullets.title: SNOW/MDB: Wolfe bullish on agentic AI growth; TimesSquare nearly doubled SNOW position
bullets.body: Wolfe ranked SNOW and MDB among top long ideas for agentic AI infrastructure. A TimesSquare PM nearly doubled their SNOW position after Cortex Code launch—over 50% of customers adopted within 9 weeks and it was not reflected in guidance. SNOW guides Q2 FY2027 product revenue at $1.41-1.42B (+30% YoY) with FY2027 at $5.84B (+31% YoY). Klein also highlighted SNOW and MDB as among the few software names likely to outperform as others struggle with AI-driven pricing shifts.

bullets.title: DLR: Three transactions totaling $1.61B; Citi/JPM maintain Buy on data center expansion
bullets.body: Digital Realty announced acquisition of 1,440 acres near Kansas City for ~$475M (600MW utility power by early 2028, up to 2GW at full buildout), increased Teraco stake to 77% for ~$650M, and acquired Columbia Capital for ~$485M. Transactions financed primarily with 6.3M shares at $197.54. Citi and JPM both maintain Buy; Citi notes Virginia's new $0.011/kWh electricity tax is manageable and largely passable to customers, with EQIX's max annual burden ~$14M and DLR's ~$79M at full ownership.

bullets.title: AFRM: Downgraded by Morgan Stanley to Equal-Weight; Mizuho raises PT on Walmart survey
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley downgraded AFRM from Overweight to Equal-Weight, saying market now properly reflects growth durability. Separately, a Mizuho proprietary survey of ~450 Walmart shoppers found Affirm preferred over Klarna at 2:1 among online-first users despite Klarna being exclusive provider for 1+ year—bullish read-through for Affirm's competitive position. Mizuho raised AFRM PT to $100 (Outperform) from prior, valuing at 6x CY27E net revenue.

bullets.title: FOXA: UBS raises F4Q EBITDA est; World Cup expected to contribute ~$500M in soccer ad revenue
bullets.body: UBS raised Fox Corp's F4Q EBITDA estimate to $1.02B (consensus $975M) driven by ~$500M in soccer advertising revenues across F4Q/F1Q (vs prior $350M estimate). Full-year FY26 EBITDA expected at a record $3.7B despite being a non-election year. Stock trades at under 5x 2027/28E standalone EBITDA or 7.7x/6.6x pro forma with Roku. FOX One app downloads up 15x+ from May to June. UBS maintains Buy.

bullets.title: CMCSA: Sky unit near deal to acquire ITV Media & Entertainment for ~£1.6B
bullets.body: Comcast's Sky unit was reported nearing an agreement to acquire ITV's Media & Entertainment business for approximately £1.6B ($2.1B USD), with ITV Studios also acquiring Love Productions. The deal would help Sky create a stronger UK streaming competitor. UBS maintained Neutral on CMCSA, modeling accelerating broadband subscriber losses (-153K in Q2) and ARPU declines (-4.0% YoY), offset by Peacock profitability and World Cup content revenue (+14% YoY).

bullets.title: SHOP: SHOP Campaigns emerging monetization driver; agentic commerce positions AMZN/GOOGL/SHOP as beneficiaries
bullets.body: UBS highlighted SHOP Campaigns/lead generation as potentially meaningful long-term growth driver via Shop app monetization; AI-referred shoppers convert 50% higher with 14% higher AOVs vs. organic search. JPM's agentic commerce report positions GOOGL, AMZN, and SHOP as primary beneficiaries, noting AI platform traffic growing 8-15x faster than industry with 2x+ conversion rates. SHOP's AI-referred orders grew 13x YoY in Q1 FY2026.
